exam.title: Differential Equations - Expert Exam
exam.subtitle: Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations
exam.instructions: Complete all tasks. Justify your steps. Permitted aids: non-programmable calculator.

exercises.title: Separation of variables
exercises.description:
Solve the initial value problems:
a) $y' = \frac{x}{y}$, $y(0) = 1$
b) $y' = ky$ with $y(0) = y_0$ (growth/decay); how long does halving take for $k = -0.1$?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Part a): Separate and integrate
$y\,dy = x\,dx \Rightarrow \frac{y^2}{2} = \frac{x^2}{2} + c \Rightarrow y^2 = x^2 + C$. With $y(0) = 1$: $C = 1$, so $y = \sqrt{x^2 + 1}$ (positive root since $y(0) > 0$).

Step 2: Part a): Check
$y' = \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+1}} = \frac{x}{y}$ ✓. The solution curves are hyperbolas $y^2 - x^2 = C$.

Step 3: Part b): General solution
$\frac{dy}{y} = k\,dt \Rightarrow y = y_0e^{kt}$.

Step 4: Part b): Half-life
$y_0e^{kT} = \frac{y_0}{2} \Rightarrow T = \frac{\ln2}{-k} = \frac{\ln2}{0.1} \approx 6.93$. Check: $e^{-0.1\cdot6.93} = e^{-0.693} = 0.5$ ✓.

exercises.title: Variation of constants
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Integrating factor
For $y' + p(x)y = q(x)$ we have $\mu(x) = e^{\int p\,dx} = e^{\ln x} = x$.

Step 2: Rearranging
Multiplying by $x$: $xy' + y = x^3$, i.e. $(xy)' = x^3$.

Step 3: Integrating
$xy = \frac{x^4}{4} + C \Rightarrow y = \frac{x^3}{4} + \frac{C}{x}$.

Step 4: Initial value and check
$y(1) = \frac14 + C = 1 \Rightarrow C = \frac34$. Solution: $y = \frac{x^3}{4} + \frac{3}{4x}$. Check: $y' = \frac{3x^2}{4} - \frac{3}{4x^2}$, $\frac yx = \frac{x^2}{4} + \frac{3}{4x^2}$; sum $= x^2$ ✓.

exercises.title: Oscillation equation
exercises.description: Solve $y'' + 2y' + 5y = 0$ with $y(0) = 1$, $y'(0) = 0$ and describe the behaviour of the solution.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Characteristic equation
$\lambda^2 + 2\lambda + 5 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 20}}{2} = -1 \pm 2i$.

Step 2: Real solutions
For $\lambda = \alpha \pm i\beta$ the real solution is $y = e^{\alpha x}(a\cos\beta x + b\sin\beta x)$, here $y = e^{-x}(a\cos2x + b\sin2x)$.

Step 3: Initial values
$y(0) = a = 1$. $y' = e^{-x}\big((-a + 2b)\cos2x + (-b - 2a)\sin2x\big)$, $y'(0) = -a + 2b = 0 \Rightarrow b = \frac12$. Solution: $y = e^{-x}\left(\cos2x + \frac12\sin2x\right)$.

Step 4: Interpretation and check
Damped oscillation: angular frequency $2$, decay factor $e^{-x}$ (since $\operatorname{Re}\lambda = -1 < 0$). Check: $y'' + 2y' + 5y$ with $y = e^{-x}\cos2x$: $y' = e^{-x}(-\cos2x - 2\sin2x)$, $y'' = e^{-x}(-3\cos2x + 4\sin2x)$; sum $= e^{-x}\big((-3 - 2 + 5)\cos2x + (4 - 4)\sin2x\big) = 0$ ✓.

exercises.title: Linear system with eigenvalues
exercises.description: Solve $\dot{\vec x} = A\vec x$ with $A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 \end{pmatrix}$, $\vec x(0) = (1,0)^T$ and classify the equilibrium $\vec 0$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Eigenvalues
$\lambda^2 + 3\lambda + 2 = (\lambda+1)(\lambda+2) = 0$: $\lambda_1 = -1$, $\lambda_2 = -2$.

Step 2: Eigenvectors
$\lambda = -1$: $A + I = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -2 \end{pmatrix}$ gives $(1,-1)^T$. $\lambda = -2$: $A + 2I = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$ gives $(1,-2)^T$.

Step 3: General solution and initial value
$\vec x(t) = c_1e^{-t}(1,-1)^T + c_2e^{-2t}(1,-2)^T$. $\vec x(0) = (1,0)$: $c_1 + c_2 = 1$, $-c_1 - 2c_2 = 0$, so $c_2 = -1$, $c_1 = 2$.

Step 4: Solution and check
$x_1(t) = 2e^{-t} - e^{-2t}$, $x_2(t) = -2e^{-t} + 2e^{-2t}$. Check: $\dot x_1 = -2e^{-t} + 2e^{-2t} = x_2$ ✓ (first equation $\dot x_1 = x_2$).

Step 5: Classification
Both eigenvalues are real and negative: $\vec 0$ is a **stable node** (all solutions tend to $\vec 0$ as $t \to \infty$). Equivalently: the ODE $\ddot x + 3\dot x + 2x = 0$ is overdamped.

exercises.title: Initial value problems with Laplace
exercises.description:
Solve with the Laplace transform:
a) $y' + y = 1$, $y(0) = 0$
b) $y'' + 4y = 0$, $y(0) = 0$, $y'(0) = 2$
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Part a): Transformation
$\mathcal{L}\{y'\} = sY - y(0) = sY$, $\mathcal{L}\{1\} = \frac1s$. So $sY + Y = \frac1s \Rightarrow Y = \frac{1}{s(s+1)}$.

Step 2: Part a): Partial fractions and inverse transform
$\frac{1}{s(s+1)} = \frac1s - \frac1{s+1}$, so $y(t) = 1 - e^{-t}$. Check: $y' + y = e^{-t} + 1 - e^{-t} = 1$ ✓, $y(0) = 0$ ✓.

Step 3: Part b): Transformation
$\mathcal{L}\{y''\} = s^2Y - sy(0) - y'(0) = s^2Y - 2$. So $s^2Y - 2 + 4Y = 0 \Rightarrow Y = \frac{2}{s^2 + 4}$.

Step 4: Part b): Inverse transform and check
$\mathcal{L}\{\sin2t\} = \frac{2}{s^2+4}$, so $y(t) = \sin2t$. Check: $y'' + 4y = -4\sin2t + 4\sin2t = 0$ ✓, $y(0) = 0$ ✓, $y'(0) = 2\cos0 = 2$ ✓.

exercises.title: Heat equation
exercises.description: Solve $u_t = u_{xx}$ on $0 < x < \pi$, $t > 0$ with $u(0,t) = u(\pi,t) = 0$ and $u(x,0) = \sin x + 2\sin3x$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Separation ansatz
Substituting $u(x,t) = X(x)T(t)$: $XT' = X''T \Rightarrow \frac{T'}{T} = \frac{X''}{X} = -\mu$ (constant).

Step 2: Boundary conditions
$X'' + \mu X = 0$ with $X(0) = X(\pi) = 0$ has non-trivial solutions only for $\mu = n^2$, $X_n = \sin nx$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$). Time part: $T' = -n^2T \Rightarrow T_n = e^{-n^2t}$.

Step 3: Initial condition
Ansatz $u = \sum_nc_ne^{-n^2t}\sin nx$. At $t = 0$: $\sum c_n\sin nx = \sin x + 2\sin3x$, so $c_1 = 1$, $c_3 = 2$, all others $0$.

Step 4: Solution and check
$u(x,t) = e^{-t}\sin x + 2e^{-9t}\sin3x$. Check: $u_t = -e^{-t}\sin x - 18e^{-9t}\sin3x$ and $u_{xx} = -e^{-t}\sin x - 18e^{-9t}\sin3x$ ✓. Boundary values: $\sin0 = \sin\pi = 0$ ✓. Higher modes decay faster ($e^{-9t}$ vs. $e^{-t}$).
